summary: L.A. Care grievance resolution letter dated May 1, 2026, annotated by Nicolas Hernandez. The annotations expose that L.A. Care completely scrubbed and omitted the Call The Car (CTC) transport grievance acknowledged in their April 1 letter. It also highlights licensing violations under the Knox-Keene Act regarding network adequacy and unlawful redirection of services to county programs.
full_text:
LA. Care

HEALTH PLAN,

For All of L.A.

May 01, 2026

NICOLAS HERNANDEZ Member Name: NICOLAS HERNANDEZ
Member ID: [REDACTED]
Reference Number: [REDACTED]47
Line of Business: Medi-Cal
Date of Service: March 30, 2026
Regarding: Quality of Service

Dear NICOLAS HERNANDEZ,

Thank you for bringing your concern(s) to our attention. L.A. Care Health Plan received your grievance on March 27, 2026. The following describes the results of our review:

Concern/s:
1. You stated that you are requesting reimbursement in the amount of $2,307 for services rendered out of network.
2. You stated that nurse practitioner Kifle Gashie Jikamo, NP, misrepresented his credentials.
3. You stated that CVS pharmacist reported medication out of stock which you believed was false.

Resolution:
1. The services in question fall under substance use disorder treatment. For Medi-Cal members, these services are a carved-out benefit. In Los Angeles, these services are administered through the Los Angeles County Department of Public Health — Substance Abuse Prevention and Control (DPH-SAPC), which can be reached at 1-800-854-7771. You may contact them to discuss your request. Per your previous grievance on November 4, 2025, you were informed that you needed to contact the Los Angeles County Department of Public Health Substance Abuse Prevention and Control (DPH-SAPC) for further assistance.
2. We have provided Carelon information regarding your grievance against NP. Please note that your concerns will be addressed.
3. L.A. Care does not manage your pharmacy benefit, please contact Medi-Cal RX program at 1-800-977-2273. This information was also communicated to you under the DMHC case number [REDACTED]55 closing letter.

1055 W. 7th Street, Los Angeles, CA 90017 | lacare.org
A public entity serving Los Angeles County

6445

--------------------------------------------------
USER ANNOTATIONS ON EVIDENCE ASSET:
--------------------------------------------------
1. [TOP ORANGE BOX OVER MARGIN]
   Annotation: "CONCERN OMITTED: L.A. Care ignored the Call The Car (CTC) portion of the grievance entirely. By refusing to document it, they attempt to void their obligation to address it. This is not an oversight; it is a calculated erasure of a valid claim."

2. [RED BOX around Concern 2 NP Jikamo credentials]
   Annotation: "Proof located in case 03 on the medical-vault page!"

3. [RED BOX and STRIKETHROUGH around CVS pharmacy stock denial "believed was false"]
   Annotation: "was false." is handwritten over "believed".
   Annotation: "Proof located in case 05 on the medical-vault page!"

4. [RED BOX around Resolution 1 (carve-out redirection to county SAPC)]
   Annotation: "Therapeutical use of benzos can cause physical dependence which is NOT the same as addiction, therefore trying to clear the queue to the county’s SUD treatment is not appropriate."
   Annotation: "Routing a customer to the county is a violation L.A. Care's Knox-Keene license agreement with the state of California. Collecting money from the state...no issue. Providing an adequate network of providers...that's another story."

5. [RED BOX around Resolution 3 (carve-out redirection to Medi-Cal RX)]
   Annotation: "Passing the buck at it’s finest...fair enough. DMHC saw the loophole as well, new filing underway!"

6. [RED CORRECTION marking out "10th floor" in the footer address "1055 W. 7th Street, 10th floor"]
   Annotation: The user crossed out "10th floor" to highlight L.A. Care's persistent use of a non-existent physical location in their directory files.
